subject: Cognitive Science
title: Top-Down vs Bottom-Up Processing
description: Learn Top-Down vs Bottom-Up Processing in one minute.

hook.text: Read this: 'Th_ c_t s_t _n th_ m_t.' You probably read 'The cat sat on the mat.' But half the letters were missing.

buildup.text: Bottom-up processing builds perception from raw sensory data—edges, colors, sounds, one step at a time.

discovery.text: Top-down processing fills in based on context, expectations, and knowledge—what you already know about cats and mats.

twist.text: Both run simultaneously and sometimes conflict. A magic trick works by making bottom-up signals contradict top-down beliefs.

climax.text: Expert radiologists see tumors that novices miss—same image, different top-down knowledge shaping perception.

punchline.text: What you see depends on what you already know.

details.summary: Bottom-up processing builds perception from raw sensory data, while top-down processing uses expectations, knowledge, and context to shape what you perceive. Most perception involves both simultaneously, with your brain constantly comparing incoming data against its predictions.
details.whyItMatters: The balance between top-down and bottom-up processing explains why experts see differently from novices and why expectations shape what we perceive.
takeaways: Bottom-up: data-driven, from senses to brain
Top-down: expectation-driven, from brain to senses
Most perception blends both processes simultaneously

faq.question: When does top-down processing dominate?
faq.answer: Top-down processing takes over when sensory data is ambiguous, degraded, or familiar. Reading messy handwriting relies heavily on context. Hearing speech in noise depends on knowing the language. Expectations fill in what the senses cannot clearly resolve.

faq.question: Can top-down processing cause perceptual errors?
faq.answer: Yes. Strong expectations can override sensory data, making you see or hear what you expect rather than what is there. Proofreading your own writing is hard because you read what you intended to write. Radiologists can miss tumors when they do not expect them.
